prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1334; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on the roadway in Baytown, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your current address and a phone number where you can be reached.

A: I'm at [address on file], and the best number is the one you already have.

Q: Walk me through what happened leading up to the impact.

A: I was stopped at a red light in the right lane. Traffic had been moving slowly, so I was maybe fifteen or twenty feet back from the car ahead of me. The light turned green, the car ahead pulled through, and I started to move.

Q: Did you feel any braking or slowing before the impact?

A: No. I was just starting to accelerate when I felt a hard jolt from behind. I don't think I had time to react at all.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you hit your head or your neck on anything during the collision?

A: My head snapped back and then forward. I hit the headrest pretty hard, and my neck felt like it was on fire right away.

Q: Have you noticed any symptoms since then?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, and I get a sharp pain going into my shoulders. I've also had headaches most days, and I've been sleeping badly.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or other medical provider for these symptoms?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening, and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week since then.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm still having trouble turning my head to check mirrors when I drive, and I'd like to get this resolved as soon as possible.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
